images.caption: Figure 1:Cinematic video generation requires inference from limited inputs and factor-aware control.(i) The man turns toward the box, places his right hand on top, and steadies the bundle with his left hand. Text-only conditioning misses this sequence, while observing the complete video enables the same model to reproduce it. (ii) Keeping the descriptions of all other factors fixed and replacing only the character-related prompt, the non-character factors change as well.These cases illustrate failures in temporal inference and factor control, with editing providing a probe of what the generator changes and preserves.

Figure 2:MLLM latents are easily bypassed in existing MLLM–DiT models.(i) Under MLLM-only conditioning, Omni-Video 2 (1.3B DiT) produces noise, while Omni-Video 2 (14B DiT) and UniVideo produce artifacts and depict one person’s successive actions as two people acting differently. MLLM latents alone therefore fail to provide reliable generation guidance in these examples. (ii) Under conflicting conditions, VAE references dominate the output.

Figure 3:Overview of Factor-Aware Predictive Learning (FAPL).Stage I freezes the MLLM and its original connector and trains the DiT using MLLM latents. Stage II retains this configuration and swaps factor-specific output spans between paired examples to supervise factor-aware changes. Stage III freezes the trained DiT and jointly updates the MLLM and connector through video reconstruction, and text-only and text-plus-complete-video inputs share the same generation target.

Figure 4:Under limited inputs, baseline models fail to predict temporal visual details.With only text and no visual references, we compare UniVideo with FAPL (Ours), highlighting representative baseline limitations across four cinematic factors.(i) Character.Long hair is generated as short hair, failing appearance details specified only by text.(ii) Scene.The background is not preserved and incorrect content appears.(iii) Action.The requested sequence,e.g., gesturing outward with the left hand and extended fingers, is missing.(iv) Camera.UniVideo ignores the instruction and keeps the camera static, while Ours orbits around the character.FAPL better realizes prompt-specified appearance, scene, and motion from text alone.

Figure 5:FAPL improves factor-aware control.For each factor, we modify only the corresponding description in the structured prompt and generate twice, comparing UniVideo with FAPL (Ours). UniVideo does not confine the change to the requested factor and alters unrelated content, whereas Ours modifies the selected factor while preserving the others.This indicates that factor-level latent augmentation enables selective control.
Figure 6:FAPL supports consistent multi-shot generation without cross-shot memory.
